Baltor · the trust engine

Models don't fail.
Their context does.

Baltor governs what becomes true: provenance, verification, signed facts, and change-data-capture. Agents propose; Baltor disposes. Nothing serves as truth until it passes the verify gate.

What Baltor does

Governed context, not guesses.

Verify before serve

Every fact is a candidate (serves_truth=false) until it passes verification against an authoritative source.

Provenance + receipts

Where each fact came from, when, and how it was checked — inspectable, with a rollback target. Lossless: raw + lineage preserved.

Stays current

Change-data-capture holds out stale facts and re-verifies when the source changes — kept-up-to-date is the wedge.

Powered by Teleon

Baltor runs on Teleon (a tenant) — trustworthy context, delivered the efficient way.

Examples

Regulated-fact verdicts you can prove.

Each is a real governed pipeline: a verdict bound to an authoritative source, with stale/overclaimed inputs held out — not an LLM guess.

Sanctions screening (OFAC)

Screen a name against the OFAC SDN list → a governed BLOCKED / CLEAR verdict with the matched entry + its source. The one place output IS truth — because it's verified.

Beneficial ownership + 50% rule

Resolve the authoritative parent from CONFLICTING ownership claims (an SEC 8-K beats a press rumor), then propagate an SDN block down every ≥50% ownership edge — an inherited block a bare model can't compute.

Drug-label claim review (FDA)

Substantiate each promotional claim against the FDA-approved label; an efficacy overclaim is HELD OUT + escalated. Flip the source → the verdict flips.

Export-control screening (BIS)

A stale vendor ‘clear’ is HELD OUT; an export to a LISTED end-user REQUIRES A LICENSE. Authority is earned, not assumed.

Why it matters

Discovery is not trust. Output is not truth.

An LLM that sounds confident is not a source. Baltor is the rail that turns proposed context into governed, provable truth — so the agents built on top can be relied on.
